nodes.summary: The cyclic polytope $C_d(n)$ is the convex hull of $n$ points on the moment curve $\gamma(\tau) = (\tau, \tau^2, \dots, \tau^d)$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$. The moment curve has order $d$: no $d + 1$ of its points lie on a hyperplane. A linear functional restricted to the curve is a polynomial of degree at most $d$, which is how its facets (Gale's evenness criterion) and its low-dimensional faces (neighborliness) are found.…

nodes.summary: Linear relations and inequalities between the face numbers $f_0, f_1, \dots$ of convex polytopes: the Euler–Poincaré relation for all polytopes, McMullen's upper bound theorem, and the passage from simplicial polytopes to simplicial spheres, where the h-vector and the Dehn–Sommerville equations live.

nodes.summary: Euler–Poincaré relation and McMullen's upper bound theorem for polytopes, and the boundary complex of a simplicial polytope as a simplicial sphere, through which the Dehn–Sommerville equations apply to simplicial polytopes.

nodes.summary: A convex polytope is the convex hull $P = \operatorname{conv} s$ of a finite set $s$ of points. Its faces are the empty set and the sets of points of $P$ at which a linear functional attains its maximum over $P$; they include $P$ itself. Ordered by inclusion they form the face lattice of $P$, a finite lattice whose isomorphism class is the combinatorial type of $P$. Every face is the convex hull of the points of…
nodes.title: Faces of convex polytopes

nodes.summary: For $n$ points spanning a $d$-dimensional affine space, the affine dependences form a vector space of dimension $n - d - 1$. Writing a basis of it as the columns of an $n \times (n - d - 1)$ matrix, the $n$ rows are the Gale transform of the configuration. Gale diagrams turn questions about polytopes with few vertices, and about projections of polytopes, into questions about low-dimensional vector configurations.
nodes.title: Gale diagrams

nodes.summary: For a natural number $d$, a set $P \subseteq \mathbb{Q}^d$ and a natural number $m$, the ordinary Ehrhart count is the number $|mP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d|$ of integer points in the dilate $mP = \{m x : x \in P\}$, where $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is viewed inside $\mathbb{Q}^d$; it is $0$ when $mP \cap \mathbb{Z}^d$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Ordinary Ehrhart count

nodes.summary: Colour the vertices of a triangulated simplex so that each vertex avoids the colours of the corners not spanning its smallest face. Sperner's lemma (1928) says that an odd number of cells, and so at least one, carry all colours. The proof is a parity argument on "doors" (faces with all colours but one), which is also a path-following argument: walking through doors from the boundary leads to a fully coloured cell.…
